result.title: Retrieval-Grounded Multi-View Reasoning for Clinically Reliable Radiology Report Generation
result.summary: Chest radiograph report generation is hampered by retrieved reports that resemble the current image but are clinically inconsistent with it, and by diagnostic-label imbalance. We present RG-MVR, a retrieval-grounded framework comprising Retrieval-Augmented Evidence Grounding, which combines dense memory summaries with visually gated sparse retrieved evidence; Adaptive Multi-view Evidential Reasoning, which weights image, memory, and retrieved evidence per case; and a Clinical Prompt Learner, which models finding mention separately from positive, negative, or uncertain status. On MIMIC-CXR, RG-MVR achieved a clinical-label F1 of 0.483 and a BLEU-4 of 0.118 (IU X-ray: 0.202 and 0.110). In an exploratory external cohort of 22 examinations, clinical-label agreement declined markedly (F1, 0.071) and unsupported statements remained common, although physicians found fewer unsupported temporal comparisons (9 vs. 20 cases) and device-related statements (7 vs. 15) than with the baseline. Evidence-aware retrieval and structured diagnostic prompting may reduce specific reporting errors, but broader external validation is required.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 RG-MVR 框架用于胸片报告生成：用稠密记忆摘要配合视觉门控的稀疏检索证据，按病例对图像、记忆与检索证据加权，并以临床提示学习器区分发现的提及与阴/阳/不确定状态，在 MIMIC-CXR 和 22 例外部队列上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 视觉门控的证据筛选与多源证据逐例加权，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选和贡献分配的做法；但文中「reasoning」实为证据加权，并无显式 latent 推理状态，外部队列的表述错误分析仅可作旁证。
